{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — RadialSpark Consulting Services Agreement

**To:** Deal Team / Business Sponsor  
**From:** In-house Counsel (Customer side — Clear Capital)  
**Re:** Playbook review of the Consulting Services Agreement with RadialSpark ("Contractor")  
**Privileged & Confidential — Attorney-Client Communication**

---

## 1. Executive Summary

We have completed our playbook review of the Agreement. Of the eighteen rules assessed, ten are compliant and require no action, six are deviations requiring redlines, and two rules are unaddressed by the document entirely.

The commercial architecture of the deal is broadly favourable to us. There is no exclusivity, no non-compete, no minimum purchase or take-or-pay commitment, no most-favoured-nation obligation, no liquidated damages or early-termination fee, no auto-renewal (the term is evergreen and exitable), and no audit right exercisable against us. Ownership of deliverables sits substantially at our preferred position — Works vest in Clear Capital with an assignment of works-in-progress on termination — and the residual licence-back of Contractor pre-existing materials is royalty-free, perpetual and sublicensable.

Our concerns concentrate in the risk-allocation provisions. Three items are, on our playbook, walk-away issues: (i) there is **no Vendor indemnity whatsoever** — Section 7 is captioned "Indemnification of Contractor" but contains only a cap, a consequential-damages waiver and a fees waiver, and the cap's sole carve-out cross-refers to Paragraph 9 (Independent Contractor), confirming the indemnity was never drafted in; (ii) the **liability cap** is measured per Statement of Work against fees actually paid, with no floor and no carve-outs for confidentiality, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud, indemnity or IP infringement; and (iii) we have **no termination-for-convenience right** while any Statement of Work is outstanding, which on an evergreen, SOW-driven engagement means no practical exit.

Secondary deviations are more readily resolved: Arizona governing law (outside our accepted list) with no venue clause at all; no assignment carve-out for our affiliates or successors; no conformity warranty, duration or remedy; no post-termination transition or data return/deletion obligation; a mutual non-solicit lacking a general-advertising carve-out; and an otherwise sound insurance covenant with no cyber/privacy coverage despite Contractor handling our data and accessing our systems.

We recommend proceeding on the basis of the attached redlines, treating the indemnity, cap carve-outs and convenience-termination right as conditions of signature.

---

## 2. Findings Table

| # | Severity | Rule | Status | Section | Summary |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Critical | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | **Missing** | § 7 (Limitations of Liability; Indemnification of Contractor) | No operative indemnity language anywhere; heading only. Walk-away territory. Inserting Contractor indemnity as new § 7(d) with claim mechanics and carve-out from § 7 limitations. |
| 2 | Critical | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | Compliant | § 4 (Ownership of Materials; Acceptance) | Works vest in Clear Capital; assignment of works-in-progress on termination; perpetual sublicensable licence-back. Substantially preferred position. Not redlined. |
| 3 | Critical | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability | **Deviation** | § 7 | Mutual, but cap measured per SOW on fees actually paid with no floor; only carve-out cross-refers to § 9 (Independent Contractor). Fails fallback. |
| 4 | High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | **Deviation** | § 7 / § 10 | Symmetrical consent standard, but no affiliate/successor carve-out for Company; fails fallback. No change-of-control trigger (acceptable). |
| 5 | High | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity binding Customer | Compliant | § 1 (Purpose of Engagement) | Task-by-task engagement via SOWs; no exclusivity or sole-supplier obligation. Preferred position. |
| 6 | High | LD — Liquidated damages / penalties on Customer | Compliant | § 6 (Termination) | No liquidated damages, penalty, minimum fee or early-termination fee. Only accrued fees on termination. Preferred position. |
| 7 | High | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | Compliant | § 4 | Royalty-free, non-exclusive, perpetual, sublicensable; no revocation right; broad business-operations scope. Meets material terms. |
| 8 | High | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete on Customer | Compliant | § 4 | No non-compete, exclusivity or field-of-use restriction on Clear Capital. Preferred position. |
| 9 | High | T4C — Termination for convenience | **Deviation** | § 6 | Convenience right available only when no SOW is outstanding; evergreen term. Fails preferred and fallback; walk-away territory. |
| 10 | Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | Compliant | § 3 (Contractor's Compensation) | No audit, inspection or verification right against us. At or above preferred by default. |
| 11 | Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | **Deviation** | § 7 / § 11 | Arizona law, outside accepted list (NY, DE, CA, England & Wales); no forum or venue provision at all. |
| 12 | Medium | MFN — Most-favoured-nation on Customer | Compliant | § 3 | No parity, price-matching or best-terms obligation. Preferred position. |
| 13 | Medium | MINCOMMIT — Minimum commitments / volume restrictions | Compliant | § 3 | Time-and-materials, task-by-task; no committed spend, shortfall or lock-in. Preferred position. |
| 14 | Medium | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation binding Customer | **Deviation** | § 7 / § 13 | Mutual, 12 months, narrow — but no general-advertising or unsolicited-approach carve-out, which the fallback requires. |
| 15 | Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and notice window | Compliant | § 1 / § 2 | No auto-renewal; evergreen term exitable on 15 days' notice when no SOW outstanding. At least as favourable as preferred. |
| 16 | Medium | TRANSITION — Transition assistance and data return | **Missing** | § 6 | No transition assistance, data return, deletion or certification anywhere; confidentiality clause imposes no return-or-destroy duty. |
| 17 | Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | **Deviation** | § 5 (Representations and Warranties; Disclaimer) | No conformity warranty, no duration, no repair/re-perform/refund remedy; no acceptance mechanic despite § 4 heading. Fails fallback. |
| 18 | Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | **Deviation** | § 7 / ¶ 14 | Workers' comp, CGL USD 1M, E&O USD 1M and certificates present (E&O at fallback). No cyber/privacy coverage despite data and system access. |

---

## 3. Walk-Away Items

The following three findings sit in walk-away territory on our playbook and should be treated as conditions of signature rather than negotiating preferences.

**3.1 No Vendor indemnity (§ 7 — INDEMN, critical, missing).** The Agreement contains no indemnity of any kind. Section 5 gives an unqualified non-infringement warranty but no defence or indemnity obligation, and the cap's only carve-out points to the Independent Contractor clause. We are asking for a Contractor indemnity as new § 7(d) covering third-party IP infringement, breach of law, unauthorised access to Company data, and gross negligence or wilful misconduct, with standard notice, control and cooperation mechanics and an express carve-out from the § 7 limitations so the indemnity is not neutralised by the cap or the fees waiver. No Customer indemnity exists, so no reciprocal narrowing is required.

**3.2 Liability cap fails the fallback on two material terms (§ 7 — LOL-CAP, critical, deviation).** Mutuality is satisfied, but Contractor's cap is measured per Statement of Work against fees actually paid for those particular Services — which on a time-and-materials engagement can fall well below twelve months' fees — with no USD floor, and there are no carve-outs for confidentiality, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud, indemnification or infringement of Company IP. Our redline sets a mutual cap at the greater of twelve months' fees paid or payable and USD 1,000,000, preserves the existing Paragraph 9 carve-out, confirms our fee payment obligation is not "damages" for cap purposes, and adds a single Excluded Claims sentence.

**3.3 No termination-for-convenience right while a SOW is outstanding (§ 6 — T4C, high, deviation).** The convenience right in § 6(a) is available only when there is no uncompleted Statement of Work; the only other exit is uncured material breach. Because the term is evergreen and SOWs are the operative vehicle for all Services, we have no convenience right for engagements running well beyond twelve months. We propose a new § 6(c) giving Company a 30-day convenience right over the Agreement and any Statement of Work, with Contractor paid only for Services performed, prepaid fees refunded, and work in progress assigned. We have left the Contractor-side 15-day right in § 6(a) undisturbed, as it can only be exercised when no engagement is active.

---

## 4. Next Steps

1. **Issue the redline** covering the six deviations and two missing rules: Contractor indemnity (new § 7(d)); mutual cap at the greater of twelve months' fees or USD 1,000,000 with Excluded Claims and exclusion of our payment obligations; Company convenience termination on 30 days' notice with refund of prepaid fees (new § 6(c)); New York governing law with exclusive venue in New York County; Company affiliate/successor assignment carve-out plus a bar on Contractor assigning to a Company competitor; a 90-day conformity-to-Specifications warranty with repair, re-performance or refund remedy; post-termination transition assistance and data return/deletion in § 6; a general-advertising and unsolicited-approach carve-out to the § 13 non-solicit; and cyber/privacy liability coverage in the insurance covenant.

2. **Confirm our fallbacks internally before the call**, so we can close efficiently: Delaware, California, or England and Wales (courts of London) if New York is resisted on governing law; 90 days of transition assistance with a 30-day export in place of six months; cyber liability at USD 2,000,000 in place of USD 5,000,000.

3. **Flag the walk-away trio to the business sponsor** — indemnity, cap carve-outs and convenience termination — and obtain sign-off that we will not execute without them.

4. **Confirm the Paragraph 9 cross-reference with Contractor's counsel.** The § 7 caption and the cap's carve-out both point to an indemnity that does not exist; we should establish whether this is a drafting omission from a precedent, which will inform how readily the new § 7(d) is accepted.

5. **Confirm the data and systems footprint with the technical owner** (Contractor personnel at our facilities and accessing our computer systems, per the Services description), as this underpins both the cyber insurance ask and the data-return obligation.

6. **Carry forward for a future amendment or SOW**, not worth blocking signature over: the IP licence-back is not styled irrevocable or worldwide and there is no standalone sentence confirming we retain all rights in Customer Data; the licence has no express successor-transfer right and affiliates/contractors are covered indirectly via sublicensing; E&O sits at USD 1,000,000 (fallback rather than preferred USD 2,000,000); § 3(b) permits Contractor to change rates on 30 days' notice with no uplift cap; the non-solicit's 12 months runs from termination of the Agreement rather than the end of the individual's involvement; and if renewal terms are ever added we should carry in the CPI/3% uplift cap."}
